name: Batavian Republic
alt: Batavian Republic and Kingdom of Holland

predecessors.name: Dutch Republic
predecessors.text: the Netherlands of the old Dutch Republic, less what the Treaty of The Hague took in May 1795

successors.name: First French Empire
successors.text: the Kingdom of Holland, abolished 'by Imperial Decree' and incorporated into the French Empire on 9 July 1810

rulers.name: Son of Louis Bonaparte (named in the abdication)
rulers.title: king

ledger.x: 19 January 1795: the Batavian Republic is proclaimed.
16 May 1795: the Treaty of The Hague cuts Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders away.
October 1801: the Batavian Republic becomes the Batavian Commonwealth (Bataafs Gemenebest).
5 June 1806: Louis Bonaparte becomes King of Holland and the republic becomes the Kingdom of Holland.
1807: East Frisia and Jever are added to the Kingdom of Holland.
1808: the capital moves from The Hague to Utrecht, and in the same year to Amsterdam.
March 1810: Holland surrenders the lands south of the Rhine to France.
9 July 1810: the Kingdom of Holland is annexed to the French Empire.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch campaign of the winter of 1794-1795
wars.outcome: 'After seizing the Low Countries in a surprise winter attack, France established the Batavian Republic as a puppet state'; Pichegru invaded in January 1795; the Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) took Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders.

wars.name: Walcheren campaign and the end of the Kingdom of Holland
wars.outcome: Holland 'had to surrender all territories south of the River Rhine to France' after the Walcheren campaign; Louis abdicated on 1 July 1810 and the kingdom was annexed on 9 July 1810.

certainty.note: The Netherlands' frontiers are the old Dutch Republic's, fixed by the Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) and the 1807 and 1810 changes; the East Frisian border of 1807 and the Rhine line of 1810 are the page's wording, not a surveyed line.
